reasons: Classification is correct: § 16.2's first and third sentences impose a blanket, unqualified consent requirement on IBM's own assignments with no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out and no reasonableness standard, which is expressly walk-away territory under ASSIGN and fails the fallback (mutual right to assign to successors on written notice).

The redline reaches the playbook position with a targeted insertion: it adds an IBM-only affiliate/successor carve-out on written notice and a not-unreasonably-withheld standard on the general consent requirement, while leaving MSL's assignments consent-gated (consistent with the preferred position that Vendor assignments require Customer consent subject to reasonableness).
The high changed-character ratio is explained by inserting a new carve-out sentence into a short clause rather than by unnecessary rewriting; the surrounding MSL sentences are preserved intact.

Rationale correctly notes that no change-of-control termination or re-pricing right runs against IBM (p0290 addresses only MSL's own sale/merger and requires successor assumption), so no further deletion was needed; the omission of the 'never to a Customer competitor' element is a minor sub-element, appropriately not treated as a separate deviation.
Comment is accurate, concise, properly prefixed, and states what changed and why with the playbook basis.
